To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cerebral arteriolar diameter changes in response to arterial blood pressure changes are mediated by two mechanisms, the metabolic and the myogenic.

the metabolic mechanisms are predominant in cerebral arteriolo regulation under normal conditions and that the myogenic mechanism can be unmasked in the presence of an oxygen-dependent metabolic vasodilation mechanism.
both myogenic and metabolic mechanisms play a role during the regulation of cerebral vascular resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cerebral autoregulatory mechanisms.
the mechanisms that control blood flow in the brain, and in the retina of the eye.
the role of oxygen in the regulation of cerebral circulation, with special emphasis on the mechanisms of cerebral autoregulatory adjustments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cerebral autoregulatory mechanism is a complex phenomenon involving several factors, including metabolic, myogenic and neurogenic mechanisms.
the cerebral arteriolar diameter is determined by a balance between the myogenic and the metabolic mechanisms.
cerebral autoregulatory mechanisms include a metabolic mechanism, a myogenic mechanism and a combination of the two.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cerebral arteriolar response to changes in arterial blood pressure is mediated by two mechanisms: the myogenic mechanism which is activated in response to stretch and is independent of changes in PO2 and metabolic mechanisms that are dependent on changes in cerebral PO2.
the cerebral arteriolar response to hypotension is dependent on the oxygen status within the brain.
the metabolic mechanism of cerebral autoregulatory vasodilation depends on the presence of a high PO2 gradient between the arterial blood and the brain parenchyma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the myogenic and metabolic mechanisms of cerebral autoregula-tion are interdependent.
the cerebral circulation can be regulated by the oxygen tension in blood and in brain.

cerebral autoregulatory mechanisms can be influenced by manipulating PO2 in the brain and that these mechanisms can be studied directly by using the pial microvascular bed as the preparation of study.
